title: QUIC and HTTP/3 System.Diagnostics.Metrics verification
verification_method: Focused MeterListener tests, HTTP/3 diagnostics regression tests, full QUIC test-project validation, build validation, SpecTrace validation, diff checks, and a focused BenchmarkDotNet disabled-listener benchmark.
scope: Verify that the QUIC and HTTP/3 Meter instruments emit representative measurements, active counters increment and decrement, tags remain bounded, disabled paths do not need diagnostics or qlog sinks, and hot datagram metric paths have negligible disabled-listener overhead.
preconditions: No collector or MeterListener is required for disabled-path operation.
The core transport does not reference qlog packages or serializers.
Metrics remain observational and do not alter protocol state transitions.
procedure: Run the focused metrics tests and confirm QUIC connection, stream, datagram, blocked, PTO, RTT, and HTTP/3 request measurements are observed.
Confirm active connection and stream measurements include positive and negative deltas.
Confirm tag keys and values remain bounded and do not include connection IDs, stream IDs, endpoints, peer addresses, paths, exception messages, or raw error text.
Confirm disabled/no-listener metric calls do not require diagnostics or qlog sinks.
Run existing HTTP/3 diagnostics tests to prove diagnostics behavior remains stable.
Run the QUIC test project and build validation.
Run the focused BenchmarkDotNet disabled-listener benchmark for datagram metrics.
Run SpecTrace core validation and git diff whitespace checks.
expected_result: The requested Meter instruments are emitted with bounded tags, active up-down counters emit matching decrement measurements, disabled metric paths do not depend on diagnostics or qlog sinks, and focused benchmark evidence shows the disabled-listener datagram path remains negligible.
